## Historical audit: S0316

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H02/development/commons_189918915/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; the supplied observations are complete lines, not split observations.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| H request, line 1 | Goal: reconstruct a single indoor photograph as editable 3D geometry with matching camera and materials. The photograph itself is not visible in this audit. |
| H response and execute, lines 3–4 | H interpreted the scene as a warehouse and built multiple assets: roof, skylight, fixtures, rack and pallet loads. Named children include beams, braces, pallet feet and wrap bands; these establish intended hierarchy, not verified physical connections. Colors and geometric seams approximate materials; no image texture is used. Camera pose, target and lens are explicit. |
| Execution result, lines 6, 8–10 | First build and render completed successfully and step 1 was selected. This verifies execution, not visual fidelity. |
| H request and response, lines 11, 13–14 | H received the reference and first render for comparison. H reported excess floor/wall, sparse pale shelving and a low, dim skylight. It raised the camera target, moved the skylight, added loads and slats, darkened beams and changed light-surface emission. These are H’s observations and causal hypotheses, not independent image verification. |
| Execution result, lines 16, 18–20 | Revised build and render completed and step 2 was selected. |
| H response and execute, lines 23–24 | After receiving the second render (line 21), H reported blank lower-right wall, steep lamp slope, low skylight and sparse foreground. It changed camera target and roll, moved the skylight and loads, extended the rack and added a load. Pose here concerns the camera and static arrangement; no articulated subject pose is evidenced. |
| Execution result and select, lines 26, 28–30 | Third build and render completed without timeout; step 3 was selected. No subsequent visual review or fidelity assessment is shown. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student receipt is present. The system and review prompts supplied general procedures, not a traceable teacher intervention. H autonomously made two render-informed revisions; its sessions reported no tool calls, while the external runner executed the programs (lines 2, 12, 22 and execution events).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Formal execution succeeded three times; final reconstruction correctness remains **unknown**, not independently established by selection, asset names or H’s descriptions. The reference and rendered images are unavailable here, so object coverage, actual part contact, textures, framing, lighting and whether the last changes improved the view cannot be checked. In particular, camera versus local geometry as the cause of the reported discrepancies remains a hypothesis.

**Lessons.** Transferably, a successful render and editable hierarchy are distinct from visual or geometric verification, and changing camera and objects together complicates causal attribution. The warehouse anchors, load placement and roll adjustments are task-specific rather than general rules.
